1 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04-05-2023 at about 3.45 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EB-4680, along with his friend as a pillion rider, from Kengeri Club to KLE Law College to go to his work, carefully by following all the traffic rules,
on the left side of the road.
from Kengeri Club to KLE Law College to go to his work.

When he reached near KEB Circle, Maruthi Nagar main road, Bengaluru, the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0093 came from Ramasandra Cross road,
with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without following the traffic rules and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Supra Hospital, Kengeri and then he was shifted to Mathru Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as Supervisor at Multiplex Urban Green India Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kengeri Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has denied the rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 in the alleged accident.
He has contended that, on 04-05-2023 at about 3.45 p.m., the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 in route No.223D/12 was on its way schedule trip from Doddabasthi to K.R. Market.

When it was proceeding near KEB Circle, Kengeri, Bengaluru and the said bus was about to take turn from the cross road to main road, the petitioner/rider of the two-wheeler bearing No.KA-40-EB-4680, who was riding the said vehicle without holding valid driving licence and without head guard, came from Kengeri Club with high speed, without observing any traffic rules and regulation and dashed against the said BMTC Bus, on the front right side of the body and caused the alleged accident and sustained alleged injuries in the alleged accident.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
He has contended that, his driver was not at all responsible for the accident and the alleged accident has occurred due to sole contributory negligent act of the rider of the two-wheeler.

The petitioner has failed to make the owner and insurer of the two-wheeler as a party in the present case, who are necessary parties and hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 04-05-2023 at about 3.45 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus, bearing registration No.
KA-57-F-0093 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.

Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Sanjukumar P.
J. and Dr. S. A. Somashekara as P.W.2 and P.W.3 respectively and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent has got examined his driver as R.W.1 and not marked any documents and closed his side.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 04-05-2023 at about 3.45 p.m., he was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EB-4680, along with his friend as a pillion rider,

10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.

3
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of Notice U/sec. 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of reply to notice U/sec. 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.9 is notarised copy of driving licence,
Ex.P.10 is authorization letter, Ex.P.11 is discharge summary, Ex.P.12 is case-sheet, Ex.P.13 is OPD record and Ex.P.14 is x-ray.
11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia

it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 and taking sudden right turn of the said bus and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-EB-4680 of the petitioner.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident and involvement of offending bus in the alleged accident is not dispute by the respondent.

The respondent has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-40-EB-4680 and dashing the same to said BMTC Bus.
But, the respondent has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is none other than the driver of offending bus at the time of accident, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondent to show that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and he himself has dashed his motorcycle to BMTC Bus.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F- 0093 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing No. KA-40-EB-4680 of the petitioner, in the process of taking right turn of the said bus.
Further it clearly reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained multiple grievous injuries all over the body.
The evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Though the learned counsel for respondent cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 40-EB-4680 himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
Hidayath.

4 13.

The Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place near KEB Circle, Maruthinagara main road, Bengaluru, due to dashing of offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-57-F-0093 to the motorcycle of the petitioner bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EB- 4680, in the process of taking right turn in the said circle.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicles Accident Report,
which is marked as Ex.P.8, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending BMTC Bus and there was no rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending BMTC Bus.

The investigation officer has also clearly stated in his final report marked as Ex.P.7 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of the accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Further, admittedly the Ex.P.7 charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or owner of the offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.11 discharge summary, Ex.P.12 case-sheet,
Ex.P.13 OPD record and Ex.P.14 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered comminuted fracture of left patella, left heel pad avulsion and fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertebra.

The same is deposed by P.W.3,
who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 04-05-2023 at about 3.45 p.m., near KEB Circle, Maruthinagara Main road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained comminuted fracture of left patella, left heel pad avulsion and fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertebra and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card and driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.8 and 9.
As per Ex.P.8 and 9, the date of birth of the petitioner is 26-12-1997.
The accident has taken place on 04-05-2023 at about 3:45 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 25 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered comminuted fracture of left patella, left heel pad avulsion and fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertebra.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 50% physical disability of left lower limb and 25% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.11 discharge summary, Ex.P.12 case sheet, Ex.P.13 OPD record and Ex.P.14 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to Hidayath.K vs B.M.T.C on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142364842/
6 note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 04-05-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 10-10- 2024, which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants and control of infection.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, the fractures of Left Patella is united with signs of infection with implants in situ.
Further, he has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the condition of the petitioner is improved.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Supervisor at Multiplex Urban Green India Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further,
he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as Supervisor at Multiplex Urban Green India Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 25 years is 18.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 15/100 X 18 = Rs.5,02,200/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has not produced any medical bills.
Further in his cross- examination, he has admitted that, the medical bills has been paid by his company.
Therefore, he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
comminuted fracture of left patella, left heel pad avulsion and fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertebra.
As per Ex.P.11 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 22 days from 05-05-2023 to 26-05-2023, in Mathru Multi-Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.

Further,

sentences.text: as per P.W.3, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.11 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 22 days from 05-05-2023 to 26-05-2023, in Mathru Multi- Speciality Hospital,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 22 = Rs.22,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.11 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 22 days in Mathru Multi-Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 22 = Rs.17,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Ramapatna Village, Mandikal Hobli,
Chikkaballapura Taluk and District, the accident has taken place near KEB Circle, Maruthinagara Main road, Bengaluru and the petitioner has taken treatment at Mathru Multi- Speciality Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 22 days as inpatient at Mathru Multi-Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 3 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore,
Rs.15,500 x 3 = Rs.46,500/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 25 years and unfortunately he has suffered comminuted fracture of left patella, left heel pad avulsion and fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertebra.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:

The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and control of infection which would cost around Rs.50,000/- in private set up.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 46,500-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 30,000-00 Total Rs. 7,28,300-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,28,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-57-F-0093 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the usage of said vehicle.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,28,300/- from the respondent, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.7,28,300/- (Rupees seven lakh twenty eight thousand three hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to Hidayath.K vs B.M.T.C on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142364842/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is none other than the driver of offending bus at the time of accident, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondent to show that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and he himself has dashed his motorcycle to BMTC Bus.
On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F- 0093 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing No. KA-40-EB-4680 of the petitioner, in the process of taking right turn of the said bus.
Further it clearly reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained multiple grievous injuries all over the body.
The evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending BMTC Bus and there was no rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending BMTC Bus.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of the accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-0093 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as Supervisor at Multiplex Urban Green India Pvt. Ltd., and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
The accident took place in 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
comminuted fracture of left patella, left heel pad avulsion and fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertebra.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
